title: Ronin Bridge exploit disclosed
description: The Ronin Bridge incident became public after a large unauthorized withdrawal involving ETH and USDC was identified.

title: Attribution to Lazarus-linked activity reported
description: Public reporting and government context associated the Ronin incident with North Korea-linked Lazarus activity.

title: Ronin users made whole and bridge liabilities reimbursed
description: Sky Mavis reported that the remaining bridge liabilities were fully reimbursed, user-backed wETH and USDC were restored 1:1, and affected users were made whole.
recovered_amount_text: 71,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC liabilities fully reimbursed by Sky Mavis
notes: Operator-funded reimbursement is recorded separately from partial attacker-fund recovery.

title: Wormhole exploit disclosed
description: The Wormhole exploit became public after unauthorized wrapped ETH minting on Solana was identified.

title: Bridge deficit backfilled
description: Public reporting described the Wormhole bridge deficit as backfilled after the exploit, enabling the record to track the incident as reimbursed/backfilled rather than unresolved.
notes: Sponsor-funded deficit backfill is classified as completed reimbursement; it is not attacker-fund recovery.

title: Wormhole included in bridge-hack research context
description: Later cross-chain bridge hack surveys use Wormhole as a major reference case for bridge exploit classification and loss-scale comparison.
notes: Used for context only, not as a primary incident source.

title: Nomad exploit disclosed
description: The Nomad Bridge exploit became public after fraudulent withdrawals were copied by many participants.

title: Partial recovery reported
description: Nomad documented returned funds and a recovery process intended to make recovered assets available to affected users on a pro-rata basis.
notes: The later restricted bridge relaunch is recorded separately.

title: Nomad included in bridge-hack research context
description: Later cross-chain bridge hack surveys use Nomad as a major reference case for message verification and bridge exploit classification.
notes: Used for context only, not as a primary incident source.

title: Harmony Horizon Bridge exploit disclosed
description: Harmony disclosed that Horizon Bridge had been exploited for roughly $100 million in assets.

title: FBI attribution to Lazarus Group reported
description: The FBI publicly attributed the Horizon Bridge theft to Lazarus Group and APT38 actors associated with North Korea.

title: Harmony Horizon included in bridge-hack research context
description: Later cross-chain bridge hack surveys use Harmony Horizon as a major reference case for bridge exploit classification and attribution context.
notes: Used for context only, not as a primary incident source.

title: Poly Network exploit disclosed
description: Poly Network disclosed a cross-chain exploit involving assets valued at more than $600 million across multiple networks.

title: Stolen funds returned in stages
description: The attacker returned the stolen assets in stages after communicating publicly with Poly Network and the wider crypto community.
recovered_amount_text: most or all reported stolen funds returned
notes: Exact final timing and asset-level reconciliation require later source-specific expansion.

title: Recovery treated as substantially complete
description: Later reporting treated the Poly Network case as a near-complete or complete recovery of the stolen funds, distinguishing it from permanent-loss bridge incidents.
notes: Needs later expansion with primary-source reconciliation details.

title: BSC Token Hub exploit disclosed
description: BNB Chain reported an irregular cross-chain transfer involving BSC Token Hub and coordinated a temporary network suspension while the exploit was contained.
status_effect: bridge exploit disclosed and network paused
notes: The nominal minted value should not be confused with the smaller amount reported as moved beyond immediate control.

title: BNB Smart Chain resumed after coordinated response
description: Validators resumed BNB Smart Chain after an upgrade and coordinated containment measures, while BSC Token Hub remained the incident focus.
recovered_amount_text: Most of the nominally created BNB did not leave BNB Smart Chain; about $100 million was later described as unrecovered.
notes: This event records network resumption, not resolution of the unrecovered amount.

title: Native BSC Token Hub path retired during BNB Chain Fusion
description: BNB Chain disabled cross-chain communication between BNB Beacon Chain and BNB Smart Chain during the final Beacon Chain sunset, retiring the historical native bridge path.
notes: The later BNB Chain Bridge aggregation interface is distinct from the retired native BSC Token Hub path.

title: Abnormal Multichain asset outflows disclosed
description: Multichain reported that assets controlled through its MPC system had moved abnormally to unknown addresses and advised users to suspend use of the service.
notes: Public estimates ranged from more than $125 million to nearly $130 million.

title: Multichain service stopped indefinitely
description: The team stated that Multichain service had stopped and bridge transactions would remain stuck on source chains, formalizing the operational suspension.
recovered_amount_text: Some centrally controlled stablecoin balances were frozen, but this is not treated as completed recovery.
notes: Suspension status is separate from final asset recovery or reimbursement.

title: Multichain announced cessation of operations
description: Multichain announced that it was forced to cease operations after losing access to operational systems and funds and after key personnel became unreachable.
notes: This seed records the team's public explanation without independently resolving legal custody or attribution questions.

title: Orbit Bridge Ethereum vault exploit disclosed
description: Orbit Chain reported that an unidentified attacker removed five asset types from the Ethereum vault and that the vault was shut down shortly after detection.
status_effect: Ethereum vault shut down after exploit
notes: Official reporting places the incident at approximately 5:52 a.m. KST on January 1, 2024.

title: Asset recovery and ecosystem normalization plan announced
description: Ozys published a draft recovery plan combining company resources, partner support, long-term support assets, and future business proceeds while acknowledging that immediate full recovery from its own resources was limited.
notes: The plan was forward-looking and is not treated as completed reimbursement or recovery.

title: XRP bridge functionality resumed after security inspection
description: Orbit Chain later reported that XRP bridge functionality had resumed after security inspection, while Ethereum-based asset migration and recovery-related work remained outstanding.
status_effect: selected non-Ethereum bridge functions partially resumed
notes: Partial service resumption does not establish full restoration of the affected Ethereum vault or user assets.

title: QBridge exploit disclosed and functions disabled
description: Qubit Finance reported an exploit of the QBridge deposit function and disabled supply, redeem, borrow, repay, bridge, and bridge-redemption functions while investigating the incident.
notes: The exploit began late on January 27 UTC and was publicly documented on January 28.

title: Qubit compensation plan announced
description: Team Mound announced that team-held tokens, debt-financed asset-management proceeds, protocol revenue, and any recovered funds would be directed toward community compensation.
amount_text: initial target tranche of at least $10 million
recovered_amount_text: stolen funds not reported as recovered
notes: The announcement was a forward-looking plan and is not evidence of completed reimbursement.

title: Qubit governance transition to DAO announced
description: The associated Bunny and Qubit protocols announced a move from development-team-led operation toward DAO governance after the exploit made the prior operating structure unsustainable.
status_effect: development-led bridge operation ended and DAO transition announced
notes: The DAO announcement covered the wider Qubit and Bunny ecosystem and did not establish QBridge reopening.

title: Qubit lending markets reopened without confirmed QBridge reopening
description: Qubit reopened new lending markets with zero initial liquidity and began compensation claims, while the reviewed announcement did not state that QBridge had resumed.
status_effect: lending markets reopened; bridge remained unconfirmed
notes: This event explicitly separates protocol-market reopening from the bridge's terminal record.

title: First THORChain ETH Router exploit disclosed
description: THORChain halted the network after the first July 2021 ETH Router incident.
status_effect: network halted after first router exploit
notes: A lower contemporary estimate of about $5 million is retained in the incident amount claims.

title: Treasury coverage and staged recovery plan announced
description: The official postmortem assigned liquidity-provider losses to treasury coverage and described a staged recovery and reopening plan.
status_effect: treasury reimbursement and recovery plan initiated
amount_text: about $16 million combined protocol insolvency across both July attacks
recovered_amount_text: liquidity-provider losses assigned to treasury coverage
notes: This shared recovery plan covers both July 2021 incidents.

title: Second THORChain ETH Router exploit disclosed
description: A second July 2021 ETH Router incident removed an ERC-20 asset basket from protocol liquidity.
status_effect: network halted after second router exploit
notes: Kept separate from the first July incident because the mechanism and asset basket differed.

title: THORChain returned to staged trading after remediation
description: After audits, router changes, node upgrades, and treasury-led loss coverage, THORChain resumed functions and trading in stages.
recovered_amount_text: protocol insolvency covered through treasury-led recovery
notes: A later expansion should pin the final staged-reopening date with a dedicated official source. Event type normalized from legacy descriptive value network_reopened.

title: GG20 TSS vault exploit disclosed
description: A May 2026 threshold-signature incident drained one Asgard vault before automatic solvency controls halted the network.
status_effect: trading halted after Asgard vault drain
notes: Later analytics described a broader total exceeding $11 million across at least nine chains.

title: TSS patch released and recovery options moved to governance
description: THORChain reported a patched release and governance review of recovery options while final loss allocation remained pending.
status_effect: patched but recovery and full reopening remained pending
notes: The official site continued to describe trading as temporarily paused during review.

title: Meter Passport false-deposit exploit disclosed
description: Meter identified unauthorized minting and reserve depletion affecting BNB and WETH representations across connected networks.

title: Postmortem and compensation plan published
description: Meter documented the false-deposit flaw and proposed PASS-token liabilities representing $4.25 million in compensation claims.

title: PASS compensation tokens distributed
description: Meter updated the postmortem to state that PASS liability tokens had been distributed to affected users under the approved compensation structure.
notes: Distribution of liability tokens is not treated as proof that all liabilities were repaid in cash or recovered assets.

title: Audited Meter Passport v1.5 went live
description: Meter reported that an audited replacement version of Meter Passport had gone live after the exploit response and redesign work.
notes: Current documentation now describes Meter Passport V2.0. Event type normalized from legacy descriptive value bridge_upgrade.

title: Allbridge Core BNB Chain pool exploit disclosed
description: Allbridge shut down bridge operations after attacks manipulated its BUSD and USDT pool accounting on BNB Chain.
amount_text: approximately $573,000 initial estimate; $650,000 later official total

title: First attacker returned 1,500 BNB
description: An attacker accepted white-hat terms and returned 1,500 BNB, representing most of the initially reported loss.

title: Compensation plan announced
description: Allbridge said affected bridge users and liquidity providers would be compensated, beginning with transactions stuck during the emergency shutdown.

title: Allbridge Core relaunch and contract changes documented
description: Allbridge documented the redesigned pool logic, contract redeployment, recovery payments, and the return of Allbridge Core service.
recovered_amount_text: most stolen funds recovered; recovery payments issued to submitted claims
notes: Event type normalized from legacy descriptive value bridge_relaunched.

title: LI.FI approval-drain exploit occurred
description: An unchecked external call in pre-bridge swap logic drained tokens from 29 Ethereum wallets with infinite approvals.

title: Vulnerability patched and all affected wallets reimbursed
description: LI.FI deployed a whitelist-based fix, reenabled swaps, disabled infinite approvals by default, and reported that all 29 affected wallets were reimbursed for a total of USD 570,000.
recovered_amount_text: 29 of 29 wallets reimbursed; USD 570,000 total operator-funded compensation
notes: LI.FI offered four larger affected users an angel-investment arrangement; one accepted it partially, and the official postmortem still reports all 29 wallets reimbursed.

title: LI.FI facet exploit disclosed and contained
description: LI.FI disabled a newly deployed vulnerable facet after unauthorized withdrawals from wallets with infinite approvals on Ethereum and Arbitrum.
status_effect: affected facet disabled and integrations paused

title: Security incident report and compensation review published
description: LI.FI attributed the vulnerability to a missing validation check introduced through human deployment error and said full-compensation options were being evaluated.
recovered_amount_text: asset tracing and recovery efforts ongoing
notes: The official report establishes containment, not the exact service-restoration point.

title: LI.FI reported continued expansion and active operation
description: LI.FI's March and April 2026 update reported new products, chain integrations, and more than 1,000 enterprise customers.
notes: This event verifies present operation; it does not resolve incident reimbursement outcomes.

title: Nomad published root-cause analysis
description: Nomad documented the initialization and message-verification flaw that allowed fraudulent messages to be accepted.

title: Nomad recovery bridge relaunched with restrictions
description: Affected users could bridge back madAssets and access pro-rata recovered funds, while new canonical-token deposits remained disabled.
amount_text: approximately $1.2 million remained in the staging wallet
notes: The relaunch did not restore unrestricted new deposits.

title: Harmony documented treasury-led recovery activity
description: Harmony reported using treasury funds to recover and burn depegged assets while community recovery work continued.
recovered_amount_text: partial buyback and burn activity reported

title: Additional Harmony recovery partner proposed
description: A community proposal described continued buyback-and-burn recovery work and sought recognition as an additional recovery partner.
notes: Evidence of continuing recovery activity, not full reimbursement.

title: ChainSwap froze the bridge after the first July exploit
description: ChainSwap reported freezing the bridge and shutting down nodes after detecting anomalous withdrawals, with a fix deployed shortly afterward.
recovered_amount_text: CORRA and RAI tokens reportedly negotiated back

title: ChainSwap announced treasury-funded compensation
description: The team said affected users would be compensated from the ChainSwap treasury and described full compensation as almost complete.
notes: Final completion is not independently established.

title: Second July exploit affected 20 bridged assets
description: A quota-logic flaw was exploited across 20 bridged assets, after which ChainSwap took the bridge offline and froze mapping tokens.
notes: Official materials describe the incident across July 10–11 UTC.

title: ASAP token replacement and compensation plan documented
description: ChainSwap described issuing a replacement token, using a pre-exploit snapshot, and compensating affected projects and holders after the second exploit.
notes: The event records the announced mechanism, not final completion.

title: ChainSwap bridge relaunched
description: ChainSwap announced that the bridge was live again after the July incidents and remediation work.
notes: Event type normalized from legacy descriptive value bridge_relaunched.

title: ChainSwap website and bridge interface remained available
description: The official ChainSwap website and bridge interface were accessible at the latest review.
notes: Availability does not establish liquidity depth or resolve historical compensation completion.

title: Celer paused the cBridge frontend after DNS hijacking reports
description: Celer detected suspicious DNS activity, took the cBridge frontend offline, and advised users to revoke approvals associated with malicious contracts.
notes: The underlying bridge contracts were not identified as the primary compromise.

title: Celer committed to compensate affected users
description: Celer's incident updates said affected users would be fully compensated following the frontend DNS cache-poisoning attack.
notes: Final compensation completion was not located in this batch.

title: cBridge frontend restored with additional monitoring
description: Celer restored the cBridge frontend after mitigation and said additional monitoring was in place.
notes: Event type normalized from legacy descriptive value frontend_restored.

title: Celer cBridge remained in active operation
description: The official cBridge interface and documentation remained available with current supported-chain information at the latest review.

title: SOCKET paused affected contracts after approval exploit
description: SOCKET reported an incident affecting wallets with approvals to the vulnerable route and paused the affected contracts while investigating and removing the route.

title: SOCKET restored service after removing the vulnerable route
description: SOCKET said the affected route had been disabled and normal bridging activity was restored after the incident response.
notes: Event type normalized from legacy descriptive value service_restored.

title: SOCKET reported recovery of 1,032 ETH
description: SOCKET reported recovering 1,032 ETH connected to the January 16 incident and said a recovery and distribution plan would follow.
amount_text: 1,032 ETH; approximately $2.3 million at the time
notes: The recovery amount is not treated as proof of final user distribution.

title: SOCKET Protocol remained active
description: The official SOCKET website and documentation remained available at the latest review.

title: pTokens bridge launched
description: pNetwork later described its first version as launching in March 2020 as the pTokens bridge for moving Bitcoin to Ethereum.

title: pBTC-on-BSC exploited and pNetwork bridges paused
description: The team stopped all bridges after detecting the pBTC-on-BSC exploit and reported 277 BTC stolen from collateral.
notes: Other pTokens bridges were not successfully drained.

title: Fix deployed and unaffected bridges gradually reactivated
description: pNetwork implemented a fix and gradually reactivated unaffected bridges after additional review and security checks.
notes: This does not establish restoration of the exploited pBTC-on-BSC bridge itself.

title: pNetwork announced a community compensation process
description: The postmortem said DAO proposals would be used to develop compensation for current pBTC-on-BSC holders.
notes: Final completion is not established.

title: pGALA contract-control issue detected
description: pNetwork identified a deployment misconfiguration, secured the Ethereum collateral, and stopped processing pGALA bridge operations.

title: pNetwork conducted an emergency whitehat pool drain
description: pNetwork minted uncollateralized pGALA to drain the vulnerable PancakeSwap pool before malicious use and ultimately collected 12,977 BNB.
status_effect: pool liquidity secured for planned redistribution
notes: The recovered BNB is not classified as stolen bridge collateral.

title: pGALA replacement and recovery plan announced
description: pNetwork described replacing the compromised pGALA contract and returning whitehat-collected BNB according to snapshots.

title: pGALA redistribution delayed
description: pNetwork said legal and compliance requirements delayed the planned 12,977 BNB redistribution.
notes: Final completion remains unverified.

title: pNetwork v2 end-of-life notice verified
description: The official pTokens application stated that pNetwork v2 had reached end of life and warned of uncertain redemption timing.
notes: The application remains reachable for risk-noticed redemption; availability is not active-service status.

title: Rainbow Bridge launched
description: Rainbow Bridge launched as a trustless, permissionless bridge connecting Ethereum and NEAR, later extending its unified interface to Aurora.

title: May fabricated-block attempt challenged
description: A watchdog challenged a fabricated NEAR block before funds could be released; the attacker forfeited a 2.5 ETH bond.
notes: The bond loss belongs to the attacker, not users or bridge reserves.

title: Two critical bridge-related vulnerabilities remediated
description: Aurora Labs received critical bug reports on June 10 and June 16 and remediated them before disclosed exploitation.
amount_text: $1 million in AURORA tokens awarded to each reporter
notes: Modeled as security context rather than exploited incident cases.

title: August fabricated-block attempt blocked automatically
description: Watchdogs challenged a fabricated NEAR block in under approximately 31 seconds; the attacker forfeited a 5 ETH safe deposit.
notes: The deposit loss belongs to the attacker, not users or bridge reserves.

title: Rainbow Bridge paused for Ethereum's Merge
description: The bridge was paused so its light client could transition safely from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake verification.
notes: Separate from both attack-attempt incidents.

title: Rainbow Bridge reactivated after Ethereum's Merge
description: Aurora said bridging was reactivated after a week of monitoring and security audits.

title: Rainbow Bridge remained active
description: Current Aurora documentation continued to describe the bridge and link to the live transfer application.

title: Synapse Protocol mainnet launched
description: Synapse expanded the earlier Nerve project into a cross-chain protocol and launched its bridge and liquidity system.
notes: The separate Nerve Bridge incident is not merged into this entity.

title: Synapse paused metapools, AMM, and bridge after nUSD manipulation
description: Synapse identified abnormal nUSD metapool pricing, paused pools across six chains, and coordinated validators to go offline.
notes: The bug was in the Saddle-derived metapool implementation, not the core bridge contracts.

title: Approximately $8.2 million nUSD transfer left unprocessed
description: Validators did not process the attacker's approximately $8.2 million nUSD bridge transaction, preserving the funds for affected liquidity providers.
recovered_amount_text: approximately $8.2 million nUSD retained for LPs
notes: The protected amount is not realized protocol or user loss.

title: Synapse restored the bridge and began pool migration
description: New pools were deployed, validators returned online, pending transactions were processed, and migration away from the vulnerable metapool design began.
recovered_amount_text: affected LP funds retained for return
notes: Final liquidity-provider distribution completion remains unverified. Event type normalized from legacy descriptive value bridge_restored_and_liquidity_migration_started.

title: Synapse bridge remained active
description: The official Synapse bridge and analytics interfaces remained available at the latest review.

title: Nerve Bridge metapools exploited
description: An attacker exploited the fUSDT and UST metapools on BNB Chain, exhausted their liquidity, and gained approximately 900 BNB according to BlockSec.

title: BlockSec published Nerve Bridge root-cause analysis
description: BlockSec attributed the incident to an inconsistent exchange-amount calculation in a Saddle-derived metapool implementation and compared it with the earlier Synapse vulnerability.

title: NerveNetwork remained operational
description: The official NerveNetwork website and documentation continued to describe active cross-chain bridge and interoperability services.

title: Holograph Operator contract exploited
description: A malicious actor used the Holograph Operator contract to mint one billion additional HLG. Holograph said it patched the initial exploit and began coordinating with exchanges and law enforcement.

title: Protocol locked and part of unauthorized supply frozen
description: Incident updates reported that the protocol was temporarily locked and that at least part of the unauthorized HLG supply was frozen through exchange coordination.
amount_text: at least 200 million HLG reported frozen in later recovery materials
notes: The exact frozen quantity and custody status require later verification.

title: Holograph announced staged HLG burn plan
description: Holograph announced a plan to remove one billion HLG through frozen exchange balances, treasury tokens, and open-market purchases; the first tranche burned approximately 53 million HLG.
recovered_amount_text: approximately 53 million HLG burned in first phase

title: Investigation attributed incident to former contractor
description: Reporting on Holograph's investigation with Halborn said a former contractor had retained or created privileged access used to mint the unauthorized supply.
notes: The reviewed source is secondary reporting on the investigation.

title: Holograph domain no longer documented the omnichain protocol
description: At review, holograph.xyz described an onchain creator-coin trading terminal rather than the 2024 omnichain tokenization protocol. The historical interoperability product is therefore treated as inactive pending stronger successor evidence.

title: Inaugural IBC connection created
description: The inaugural IBC connection was created between Cosmos Hub and IRISnet, beginning production use of the protocol.

title: First IBC token transfer completed
description: The first IBC token transfer was sent between IRISnet and Cosmos Hub.

title: Dragonberry vulnerability discovered
description: Engineers discovered that forged absence proofs could enable forged IBC timeouts and potentially escalate to ICS-20 double-spends against escrow accounts.
notes: Official retrospective states that vulnerability discovery was not itself an exploitation incident.

title: Dragonberry private patch coordination began
description: Core teams coordinated confidentially with validators and chain teams. A network became resistant to undetected exploitation once more than one-third of voting power had patched.

title: Public Dragonberry and Elderflower patches released
description: Cosmos SDK and ibc-go patch releases were published for supported release lines, and chains were urged to upgrade immediately.

title: Dragonberry retrospective confirmed no funds lost
description: The official retrospective explained the forged-timeout risk, patch thresholds, and coordination process, and stated that no funds were lost from Dragonberry or the accompanying Elderflower issue.

title: Huckleberry full-node vulnerability disclosed
description: The ibc-go team disclosed a vulnerability affecting all versions of ibc-go. It was generally low severity but could become high or critical depending on full-node architecture.
amount_text: No known exploitation or loss reported

title: Huckleberry patches released across supported ibc-go lines
description: Patch releases were issued for supported v4, v5, v6, and v7 ibc-go lines, with corrected v4 builds published after an initial release mistake.

title: IBC remained active with supported v10 and v11 release lines
description: The official IBC site remained active, and the ibc-go repository listed supported v10 and v11 release lines with a May 2026 v11.1.0 release.

title: RenVM mainnet launched
description: Ren released RenVM Mainnet SubZero and RenBridge support for minting native assets such as BTC on Ethereum.

title: RenBridge 3.0 launched
description: Ren announced RenBridge 3.0 with host-chain-to-host-chain asset transfers across supported networks.

title: Ren 2.0 announced
description: Ren introduced a planned community-run Ren 2.0 architecture and described future testnet, Chaosnet, and mainnet stages.

title: Ren 1.0 sunset announced after Alameda funding ended
description: Ren said the development team would lose Alameda-related funding after Q4 2022 and announced an accelerated Ren 1.0 sunset process.

title: Mint-disable and temporary burn-only transition announced
description: The sunset plan called for Ren 1.0 mints to be disabled while burns remained available for approximately thirty days before shutdown.

title: Ren 1.0 remained historical and Ren 2.0 remained coming soon
description: The current Ren Foundation page described Ren 1.0 as the historical network and Ren 2.0 as coming soon, without evidence of a public successor mainnet.

title: Avalanche-Ethereum Bridge launched
description: Avalanche's first official Ethereum bridge entered production, connecting Ethereum assets with Avalanche C-Chain.

title: Next-generation replacement announced
description: Avalanche announced preparation for a faster, lower-cost successor bridge and planned migration of existing AEB assets.

title: Avalanche Bridge replaced AEB
description: The SGX-based Avalanche Bridge launched as the official replacement for the Avalanche-Ethereum Bridge.

title: AEB relayers and transfers were sunset
description: Official migration material described permanent disabling of AEB transfers, movement of held assets to the successor wallet, and token-upgrade support.

title: Legacy AEB asset upgrade support remained available
description: Avalanche support documentation continued to explain how holders could swap deprecated AEB token contracts into current bridgeable assets.

title: Avalanche Bridge launched
description: Avalanche launched the new SGX-based bridge for transfers between Ethereum and Avalanche C-Chain.

title: SGX and Bridge Node architecture documented
description: Avalanche published a technical explanation of the SGX enclave, Bridge Nodes, threshold operation, and migration from AEB.

title: Avalanche Bridge remained operational through Core
description: Current Avalanche support documentation described active ETH and ERC-20 transfers between Ethereum and Avalanche C-Chain through the Core bridge interface.

title: ShuttleFlow security audit announced
description: Conflux announced that PeckShield had completed a security audit of the ShuttleFlow cross-chain asset protocol.

title: ShuttleFlow multi-chain role documented
description: Conflux described ShuttleFlow as a transit-chain based multi-asset bridge connecting assets and infrastructure across DeFi networks.

title: ShuttleFlow v1.3.0 frontend released
description: Conflux released a major ShuttleFlow frontend upgrade for cross-chain asset operations.

title: ShuttleFlow closure and Zero Gravity migration announced
description: Conflux announced transfer of ShuttleFlow technology and bridge operations to Zero Gravity and provided a staged shutdown schedule.

title: ShuttleFlow bridge service ended
description: The announced bridge service end took effect and remaining users were directed to Zero Gravity, while a limited ShuttleFlow claim function remained available.

title: ShuttleFlow website and dApp shutdown date reached
description: The official transition schedule ended the residual ShuttleFlow website, dApp, and limited claim path after the migration period.

title: Transit Swap routing exploit occurred
description: Attackers used an unchecked routing and permissions path to transfer assets from wallets that had approved the affected Transit Swap contract.
amount_text: USD 21 million to USD 28.9 million reported scope
notes: This is an aggregator routing and approval incident, not an underlying bridge-reserve compromise.

title: Transit Swap incident disclosed and traced
description: Transit Finance and security firms disclosed the incident, traced attacker addresses, and began communicating for asset return.
amount_text: initial public estimates near USD 21 million to USD 23 million

title: Main attacker returned approximately 70 percent
description: Security analysis and reporting stated that the main attacker returned approximately 70 percent of the initially reported stolen assets.
recovered_amount_text: approximately 70 percent of the initial reported amount returned
notes: Attacker return is not protocol-funded reimbursement.

title: Additional BNB returns reported
description: SlowMist's incident record reported additional BNB returns after an agreement with the principal attacker, while other actors and final reconciliation remained separate.
recovered_amount_text: additional BNB returned; final aggregate unresolved
notes: Do not infer full recovery from the principal-attacker agreement.

title: Swap and cross-chain services formally suspended
description: Transit Finance announced that swap and cross-chain swap services were suspended while technical upgrades continued.

title: Transit Swap relaunched after contract replacement
description: Transit Finance restored swap and cross-chain functions after changing approval handling, whitelisting external calls, hardening bridge interactions, abolishing old-contract authority, publishing replacement contracts, and completing a SlowMist audit.
notes: Relaunch does not establish completed restitution for every affected user.

title: MagpieRouterV2 exploit occurred
description: An attacker exploited selector-position validation in MagpieRouterV2 and drained approved assets from 221 wallets.
notes: The incident affected Magpie's router and approved user assets, not Wormhole's bridge reserves.

title: Magpie dApp paused during incident response
description: Magpie paused and shut down the dApp to stop additional losses while the vulnerable routing path was fixed.

title: All affected Magpie users reimbursed in full
description: Magpie reported that every affected wallet had been reimbursed with the original asset on the chain where the loss occurred.
notes: This is reimbursement, not attacker return or recovered stolen funds.

title: Magpie published router-vulnerability postmortem
description: The first-party postmortem described the selector-position flaw, temporary mitigation, permanent fix, reimbursement, and planned audit and monitoring work.

title: Magpie returned to operation after remediation
description: A May 2024 first-party follow-up described the vulnerability as fixed, users as fully refunded within two weeks, and the protocol as safe to use while additional audits and monitoring integrations continued.
notes: Month precision is used because a dedicated exact-date relaunch notice was not located.

title: Rubic native RBC/BRBC bridge disabled
description: Rubic reported that its native RBC/BRBC bridge was disabled at the end of October and replaced in practice by an external bridge solution.

title: RBC/BRBC bridge wallet compromise occurred
description: Unauthorized actions using a compromised administrative-wallet private key released assets associated with the former RBC/BRBC bridge.

title: Rubic disclosed token sales and attacker proceeds
description: Rubic reported approximately 35 million RBC/BRBC sold and approximately 138 ETH proceeds remaining in the marked attacker wallet.

title: Rubic announced tokenomics relaunch after collateral break
description: Rubic stated that the additional RBC supply broke the RBC/BRBC collateral relationship and proposed relaunching the token with new tokenomics.

title: RubicProxy approval exploit occurred
description: An attacker abused RubicProxy routing validation and approved user allowances to transfer USDC and convert it to ETH.

title: Rubic stopped affected contracts and warned users
description: Rubic stopped affected contracts and advised users to revoke approvals while the exploit was investigated.

title: Rewritten Rubic contracts entered production
description: Later first-party contract documentation stated that rewritten and audited Rubic contracts launched in April 2023.

title: Rubic published updated security architecture
description: Rubic described rewritten contracts, audits, multisignature management, server hardening, monitoring, a CISO function, and a planned bug bounty.

title: Unizen external-call approval exploit occurred
description: An unsafe external-call path exposed assets approved to the affected Ethereum trade-aggregation contract.

title: Unizen incident and approval risk disclosed
description: PeckShield and Unizen communications warned users about the approval issue and the need to revoke the affected contract allowance.

title: Unizen offered bounty and engaged investigators
description: Unizen sent an on-chain message offering a 20 percent bounty and stated that law-enforcement and forensic specialists were involved.

title: Unizen announced immediate reimbursement plan
description: Unizen announced that more than 99 percent of affected users would be made whole, beginning with wallets losing USD 750,000 or less, while larger cases would be handled individually.
amount_text: wallets at or below USD 750,000 prioritized

title: Unizen reimbursement distributions began
description: The official announcement stated that distributions would begin immediately using USDT or USDC and would be reviewed wallet by wallet.

title: Unizen reported partial recovery from four hackers
description: SlowMist reported that Unizen's CTO announced approximately USD 185,000 recovered from four hackers.

title: Unizen deployed critical updates and resumed operation
description: First-party and contemporaneous reporting described critical contract and application updates, while current documentation and audits support continued active operation.

title: Remaining stolen funds moved through Tornado Cash
description: Later tracking reported the exploiter moving approximately USD 2.16 million in stolen funds through Tornado Cash, preventing any inference of full attacker return.

title: Forged Taiko bridge messages accepted on Ethereum
description: Compromised verification allowed fraudulent messages without legitimate source-chain events to release assets through the first-party bridge path.

title: Taiko halted network and bridge operations
description: Taiko halted block production and stopped first-party bridge and ERC20Vault withdrawals during containment.

title: Bridge withdrawals suspended
description: Taiko warned that bridge withdrawals were not secure during containment and suspended the affected first-party paths.

title: Taiko estimated losses before containment
description: Taiko estimated approximately USD 1.7 million in losses before the pause stopped further fraudulent withdrawals.

title: Taiko recollateralized bridge and reviewed fixes
description: Taiko closed the attack path, reviewed fixes with independent specialists, and restored one-to-one backing before reopening.
notes: Recollateralization is not attacker-fund recovery.

title: Taiko Bridge reopened
description: Taiko stated that the network and bridge were restored and the bridge was open with conservative withdrawal quotas.

title: Taiko stated all affected users were made whole
description: The first-party reopening statement said every affected user had been made whole.

title: Conservative withdrawal quotas retained
description: Taiko retained temporary withdrawal quotas as a post-reopening safeguard.
notes: The safeguard does not by itself establish current limited status after later active verification.

title: Connext protocol launched
description: Connext began as cross-chain and payment-channel infrastructure and later evolved into a broader interoperability protocol.

title: xPollinate renamed Connext Bridge
description: Connext consolidated its flagship xPollinate bridge interface under the Connext Bridge name.

title: Connext adopted the Everclear identity
description: Connext announced its evolution into Everclear and a clearing-layer model for cross-chain liquidity and solver rebalancing.

title: Everclear Mainnet Beta launched
description: Everclear launched Mainnet Beta for its clearing-layer protocol.

title: Everclear full mainnet launched
description: Everclear announced full mainnet operation with additional chain support and protocol incentives.

title: Everclear protocol, UI, and chain sunset
description: The wind-down announcement described the protocol, user interface, and chain as already sunset and no longer operational.
notes: Month precision avoids assigning one unsupported exact effective day to every component.

title: Everclear Foundation and Labs wind-down announced
description: Everclear announced the wind-down of Foundation, Labs, and product-development operations after failing to reach sustainable commercial depth.

title: Commons Bridge proxy compromised
description: The Commons Bridge proxy on Base was compromised, enabling unauthorized control or removal of approximately 18.45 million SYND.

title: Syndicate disclosed Commons Bridge compromise
description: Syndicate disclosed the bridge compromise, began tracing the attacker, and advised users not to provide liquidity during response.

title: Commons Bridge operations paused
description: Commons Bridge operation and related liquidity activity were paused during containment and investigation.

title: Syndicate began tracing and security investigation
description: Syndicate engaged security firms and began tracing attacker activity while assessing reserves and affected users.

title: Syndicate committed reserves for affected users
description: Syndicate stated that sufficient SYND reserves were available to help affected users while the incident response continued.

title: Commons users automatically reimbursed
description: The official shutdown page states that every SYND balance on Commons, including staked SYND and unclaimed rewards, was returned to the corresponding Base wallet plus an additional 15 percent.

title: Commons network and bridge wind-down announced
description: Syndicate announced the Commons wind-down alongside the Labs lifecycle update and reimbursement outcome.
notes: The operator stated that the bridge compromise did not cause the separate Labs wind-down decision.

title: Commons Bridge permanently shut down
description: The official Commons page states that Commons has shut down and no user claim action is required.

title: Ronin Bridge reopened after audits and recapitalization
description: Ronin reported that the rebuilt bridge was open for deposits and withdrawals after internal and external audits and full backing of user balances.

title: Wormhole service restored after deficit backfill
description: Wormhole announced that funds had been restored and the bridge service was operational again after the sponsor-funded deficit backfill.
notes: Reopening is recorded separately from the deficit-backfill reimbursement event.

title: Poly Network upgraded mainnet and began restoring cross-chain service
description: Poly Network reported that its upgraded mainnet was live and cross-chain functionality had begun returning for supported assets under a staged restoration process.

title: Poly Network completed its operations-resumption roadmap
description: Poly Network later reported that the roadmap for resuming operations and restoring user assets had been completed, after cross-chain services and advanced functions were progressively restored.

title: BSC Token Hub cross-chain transfers re-enabled after urgent patch
description: BNB Chain deployed an urgent cross-chain infrastructure patch and reported that previously paused cross-chain transfers would be re-enabled after the upgrade took effect.
notes: This bridge-specific event is separate from the BNB Smart Chain validator pause and resume.

title: THORChain returned to staged trading after 2021 remediation
description: THORChain returned to staged trading after the July exploit response and protocol hardening work; this event links the shared operational restart to the first ETH Router incident.
notes: The same operational restart period also applies to the second July 2021 ETH Router incident.

title: THORChain reported 2021 exploit users fully reimbursed
description: THORChain stated that after the chain restarted, liquidity providers and node operators affected by the 2021 exploits were fully reimbursed approximately 16 million dollars in aggregate.
recovered_amount_text: approximately $16 million reimbursed across the combined 2021 exploit aftermath
notes: The official aggregate amount is not split between the two July incidents.

title: THORChain reported 2021 exploit users fully reimbursed
description: THORChain stated that after the chain restarted, liquidity providers and node operators affected by the 2021 exploits were fully reimbursed approximately 16 million dollars in aggregate.
recovered_amount_text: approximately $16 million reimbursed across the combined 2021 exploit aftermath
notes: The official aggregate amount is not split between the two July incidents.

title: Allbridge recovery payments completed for submitted claims
description: Allbridge reported that recovery payments had been provided to all affected users who submitted the application form after most stolen funds were recovered.
recovered_amount_text: recovery payments to all affected users who submitted the application form
notes: The completion scope remains qualified to users who submitted the application form.

title: ChainSwap bridge relaunched after the July incident period
description: ChainSwap announced that its bridge was live again after integrating with Anyswap and completing the post-July remediation period.
notes: This records the later final relaunch after the combined July remediation period; it does not claim a durable reopening before the second exploit.

title: Allbridge Core Solana pool exploit disclosed
description: Allbridge disclosed a security incident affecting Core, paused the protocol, told affected liquidity providers to withdraw, and subsequently confirmed that an attacker had withdrawn $1.65 million from Core liquidity pools.
notes: The later relaunch is represented at incident level in this batch because the first-party Telegram rendering proves reopening but does not expose an independently stable calendar date for a separate reopen event.

title: Five billion SYS returned and burned after bridge exploit
description: Syscoin's June 15 technical postmortem confirmed that the 5 billion SYS released without authorization on June 7 had been returned to the official recovery address and then burned to a standard OP_RETURN, restoring the reported coin supply, while the bridge remained paused.
status_effect: full fund recovery; bridge remained paused
notes: Month precision is intentional: the postmortem proves the full recovery/burn by June 15 but does not assign one exact calendar date to the completed milestone.

title: TAC Inner Bridge exploited and TON/TAC framework paused
description: TAC's sequencer set accepted a bridge message from a counterfeit TON jetton wallet because the software did not verify canonical code-hash and expected-minter provenance. Unbacked equivalents were minted on TAC and used through the legitimate return path to release real locked assets on TON; TAC halted the TON/TAC cross-chain framework after confirming the breach.
notes: The event date follows TAC's incident timeline. Foundation shortfall coverage was announced later and is represented at incident level rather than treated as completed reimbursement.

title: TAC recovery arrangement returns majority of affected assets
description: TAC's tracing appendix records May 14 refund transactions after a negotiated recovery arrangement. TAC later reported final net recovered funds of $2,290,687.90, approximately 80.2% of the $2,854,486.22 protocol loss; the bridge remained paused and the Foundation committed to cover the remaining shortfall.
status_effect: partial fund recovery; bridge remained paused
notes: May 14 is the first-party refund-transaction date from Appendix II. The later final net recovery calculation is retained in the event description without converting the Foundation backstop into completed reimbursement.
